page.layout: One column of running text. Running head at the top, page number at the top right. Greek quotation set as indented lines. Verse heading and verse stanza in the lower half. Catchword and signature at the foot.

main_text.p: studio ἐπιχαραγαθίαν[?] sectandam esse: ne isti peruerso sæculo filii lucis configuren-tur. Rom.12.2.
Cum boni affliguntur, eorum miserari: cum iisdem res fecundæ sunt, gaudere oportet. i.Cor.13.
Cum mali affliguntur, itidem miserari decet, & cum in rebus fecundis luxuriant eorum animi. Sciunt enim, in aduersis quidem solida consolatione, in fecundis uero & stabili gaudio eos destitui.
Vere itaque gaudeamus cum gaudentibus: Rom.12.15. nam charitas non inuidet: 1.Corinth.13.4. & abfit a nobis fucus simulationis & dissimulationis, de quo Æschylus ficticium congaudium depingens, ait:
τῷ ἀντιφαγήντι[?] δ' ἐπιφθονάχαι[?] ὡς τις ἑτοίμος[?], ἀλγμα[?] δὲ λύπης ἐν ἦμαρ[?] προσαινέτω[?]:
ὧν νύντι δὲ χαίρει[?] ὁμοιοπρεπῆς[?] ἀγέλαστα[?] πρόσωπα[?] βιαφθέγγοι[?].
main_text.head: VERSVS XVII.

p.i: Quandoquidem rapina quam fecisti in Libano, obruet te: & praeda illata a feris, conteret eas, propter sanguinem hominum, & uio

page.notes: The Greek lines are the least certain part of the page; every word of them is marked [?] because the scan is small and smudged. Letters in the first Greek line, such as ἐπιχαραγαθίαν, may be misread. Last verse line is cut off by the catchword at the foot: "uio" is printed as the catchword, so the rest of the line is not on this page. Long s was read as plain s throughout, and the printed "j" in "filij" and "ijsdem" was normalised to i as the rules require. The word "configuren-tur" keeps its printed hyphen at the line end.
